location: Monte Fitz Roy seen from the El Chaltén area, Los Glaciares National Park, Santa Cruz
alt: Sunrise light on the granite spires of Monte Fitz Roy above the Patagonian steppe near El Chaltén
caption: First light on Monte Fitz Roy, the granite skyline that El Chaltén is built under. The Laguna de los Tres hike on days 6-7 is timed to reach this view at dawn, weather permitting.

location: Perito Moreno Glacier, Lago Argentino, Los Glaciares National Park
alt: The blue-white front of the Perito Moreno Glacier meeting the milky waters of Lago Argentino
caption: The terminus of the Perito Moreno Glacier, one of the few Patagonian glaciers that is roughly in balance. The steel boardwalks opposite the 60-m ice wall are the day-3 centrepiece.

location: Laguna Torre and Cerro Torre, Los Glaciares National Park (El Chaltén sector)
alt: Cerro Torre and its east face rising behind the glacial lake Laguna Torre
caption: Cerro Torre above Laguna Torre, the easier and more sheltered of the two classic Chaltén day hikes. It is the day-5 hike and the fallback when the Fitz Roy side is clouded in.

attribution: Fernando — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Perito Moreno Glacier, Los Glaciares National Park
alt: A roped group of walkers wearing crampons crossing the ice surface of the Perito Moreno Glacier
caption: Guided crampon walking on the Perito Moreno ice. Only licensed operators may take visitors onto the glacier, so this is the one day-3 activity that is booked in advance and priced separately.

location: Laguna de los Tres, Los Glaciares National Park (El Chaltén sector)
alt: The Fitz Roy massif above the turquoise glacial lake Laguna de los Tres
caption: Laguna de los Tres at the foot of Fitz Roy, reached by a final steep climb above the Poincenot camp. This is the trip's physical high point and its most weather-dependent view.

attribution: Almonroth — CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: The small mountain town of El Chaltén in its valley beneath the Andes
caption: El Chaltén, a trekking village of a few thousand people founded for border and tourism reasons. It is the base for days 4-8, with guesthouses, supermarkets and private campsites.

attribution: Miguel — CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Southern shore of Lago Argentino, near El Calafate, Santa Cruz
alt: Lago Argentino and the far-shore Andean peaks framed by a dark rock arch
caption: Lago Argentino through a rock arch on its southern shore near El Calafate, with the ice-capped Andes on the far side. The lake feeds the Perito Moreno front, and the town on its shore is the arrival airport, shop and car-rental base.

alt: Open Patagonian steppe and a river valley with a mountain flank near El Chaltén
caption: The steppe and river valley at the edge of El Chaltén, typical of the country crossed on the 215-km drive from El Calafate. The road is paved but wind-exposed, and guanacos and rheas are common beside it.

attribution: Justraveling.com — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Les Eclaireurs Lighthouse, Beagle Channel, Ushuaia
alt: The red-and-white Les Eclaireurs lighthouse on a small rocky islet in the Beagle Channel
caption: Les Eclaireurs lighthouse on its islet in the Beagle Channel, the usual turnaround point of the Ushuaia boat trips on day 11, with sea lions and cormorants on the neighbouring rocks.

caption: Lago Roca, signed Lago Acigami, a Yámana word the signboard glosses as a long woven basket. It is the one place on the Ushuaia leg where the Indigenous Yámana presence is spelled out on site; day 10 pairs it with the Senda Costera shore walk.

alt: The green glacial lake Laguna Esmeralda in a peat-and-beech valley above Ushuaia
caption: Laguna Esmeralda, reached by a boggy valley trail from the Ushuaia road. It is a half-day option on day 11 that needs waterproof boots rather than any technical skill.
